description: Measures that later stages compute and report. Each metric names the fields it reads, how it is worked out in words, and what the data shows today. No metric has a target value. A PROPOSED bound from the baseline is recorded as a note with Owner: Team-Force. It is not a target.

metrics.name: tokens per invocation
metrics.description: How many tokens one model call used.
metrics.formula: The token figure stored on one call row. For a set of calls, the sum of token figures divided by the number of calls.
metrics.live_source: Before stage S04-09, the live body returned token_estimate, computed as len(prompt.split()) * 2. The value for REC-0001 was 64. The gateway does not write the CSV, so the two figures never meet. Now (S05R, 1.1.0): the body field is tokens and the audit row has the key tokens, with token_estimate_method word_count_x2_EDUCATIONAL. The formula is the same and the number is EDUCATIONAL, because it is a word count doubled. The figure of 64 for REC-0001 described the old prompt. The prompt text changed in stage S04-09, so that figure is no longer current.
metrics.today: The CSV holds 353 numeric token_count values. The SIMULATED sum in the cost envelope is 845675. That sum is a lab figure.

metrics.name: cost per correlated incident
metrics.description: How much the model calls for one incident cost, once alarms have been tied to that incident.
metrics.formula: The sum of cost figures for the calls whose incident_id is this incident, divided by one incident. Cost comes from events cost_units or from a hosted-model price that is Unknown.
metrics.today: The join from alarms to incidents is Unknown, so no incident is correlated yet. events.jsonl has cost_units with an Unknown money unit. The hosted-model price is Unknown. This metric cannot be computed today.

metrics.name: quarantine rate
metrics.description: The share of rows a batch held aside as bad instead of passing them on.
metrics.formula: Rows held aside divided by rows processed, for one batch run.
metrics.today: etl/run_daily_batch.py printed processed 354 and malformed 1. It held nothing aside. It writes no file of bad rows. So the rate today is 0 of 354, while 1 row is known bad. Where a held-aside row would go is Unknown. Now (S05R, 1.1.0): the batch prints a fourth value, quarantined, which counts every row held aside, and it names each such row on stderr by file line (stage S04-11, rule.bad_row_held_aside_batch_goes_on). It still writes no file, and the count is not stored. A stored place for the count is deferred to Team-Force.

metrics.name: retry count
metrics.description: How many times a service order build was tried again.
metrics.formula: The retry_count value on one order row. For a set of orders, the minimum, maximum, and the count at or above a bound.
metrics.today: 353 numeric values. Minimum 32. Maximum 4995. 294 at or above 1000. ORD-00002 has 4052.
metrics.proposed_bound_note: The baseline uses 1000 as a PROPOSED bound so the odd case is counted. Owner: Team-Force. It is not an approved maximum and not a target.

metrics.name: audit completeness
metrics.description: How much of a full decision record each audit row holds.
metrics.formula: For one audit row, the count of required fields that are filled divided by the count of required fields. Required fields are ts, action, actor, correlation_id, record_id, and, for a model call, model, approval_id, and policy_result.
metrics.live_source: Before stage S04-08, logs/audit.log rows held ts, action, and details. details held record_id and role for a read, and record_id and model for a summary. Now (S05R, 1.1.0): a row has the 15 keys in concept.audit_row. The row has no record_id key. Stages S04-08 and S04-12 made that change.
metrics.today: Before stage S04-08, a record.read row filled ts, action, record_id, and a role string. An ai.summary row filled ts, action, record_id, and model. No row had actor, correlation_id, approval_id, or policy_result. Now (S05R, 1.1.0): every row fills ts, correlation_id, role, action, and resource. A row fills actor when the role maps to a persona. A model call fills model, model_version, prompt_hash, tokens, and latency_ms. The keys approval_id and policy_decision are null on every row. The key record_id does not exist, so the formula below cannot count it. The fix is deferred to Team-Force. The audit gap report (AG-01) counts 96 old three-key lines in the log.
metrics.required_fields_note: The required-field list above is PROPOSED. Owner Team-Force. Stage S05-14 confirms it. The repo does not define a full decision record.

metrics.name: recommendation latency
metrics.description: How long a model call takes from request to answer.
metrics.formula: The time the answer arrived minus the time the request was sent, in milliseconds, for one call.
metrics.live_source: Before stage S04-09, the live gateway waited time.sleep(0.01) and returned. It recorded no latency on the body or the audit row. Now (S05R, 1.1.0): the body field latency_ms and the audit row key latency_ms hold the milliseconds of the model call when the model ran. The model is a stub, so the figure is SIMULATED.
metrics.today: events.jsonl holds latency_ms on every line. Before stage S04-09, no live call recorded it. Now (S05R, 1.1.0): every live call that reached the model records it. Report the 95th percentile (p95): 95 of every 100 calls finish at or under that time. Team-Force decided this in ADR 0002 on 2026-10-12 (D-16). It names a method and sets no target, so target stays null.

metrics.name: SLA breach risk
metrics.description: A stored score for how likely the service promise on an incident will be broken.
metrics.formula: The sla_breach_risk value on one incident row. The repo does not say how the score is made.
metrics.today: 352 values between 0 and 1. INC-00019 holds 1.42. One cell blank.
metrics.proposed_bound_note: The baseline uses 0 to 1 inclusive as a PROPOSED range. Owner: Team-Force. It is not an approved range and not a target.

metrics.name: alarm storm size
metrics.description: How many alarms share one storm batch.
metrics.formula: The count of alarm rows with the same storm_batch_id, after rows with the same dedupe_key are counted once.
metrics.today: 351 distinct storm_batch_id values. Three appear twice. The largest batch in the file is 2 rows. How many alarms make a storm is Unknown.

metrics.name: AI outcome count
metrics.description: How many model calls ended in each of the four outcomes.
metrics.formula: For each outcome word, the count of calls whose outcome field holds that word.
metrics.today: Before stage S04-09, no live call recorded an outcome. The CSV columns guardrail_status and approval_required hold the generic status words, not the four outcome words. Now (S05R, 1.1.0): the audit key outcome holds RECOMMEND_ONLY, HOLD_FOR_REVIEW, or BLOCK on a summary call, and holds null on a record read. The metric reads the audit key outcome in practice. EXECUTE never appears, because no route reaches it. The source_fields list stays as written.

metrics.name: API availability
metrics.description: How often a call to the API got a useful answer instead of a failure.
metrics.formula: The calls that did not fail divided by all calls, over one period. What counts as a failed call is Unknown. A refusal by the policy (HTTP 403) is a designed answer, and whether it counts as a failure is Unknown.
metrics.today: The repo stores no count of health calls, no count of failed calls, and no uptime series. An audit row is written by the business routes and not by /health. Availability is Unknown.

metrics.name: record read latency
metrics.description: How long one record read takes inside the server, before the response leaves.
metrics.formula: The time domain_service.load_record takes for one call, in milliseconds. For a set of calls, the median.
metrics.today: Stage S04-10 (SR-01) reads devices.csv once and keeps an index by device_id. The design in docs/10-performance/scaling-recommendations.md names an engineering check of at most 0.1 ms per call. That check is not a service level.
metrics.proposed_bound_note: The scaling design uses 0.1 ms as an engineering check. Owner: Team-Force. It is not an approved service level and not a target.

metrics.name: repeated prompt share
metrics.description: The share of model calls whose prompt matches the prompt of an earlier call.
metrics.formula: The audit rows whose prompt_hash equals the prompt_hash of an earlier row, divided by the audit rows that hold a prompt_hash. Two prompts match when the SHA-256 hashes are equal.
metrics.today: Rows that reached the model hold a prompt_hash. The repo does not compute this share. A saving from a stored answer is Unknown until a store exists, and no store exists.

metrics.name: cost per flow
metrics.description: How much the steps of one business flow cost, for each of the four flows.
metrics.formula: The sum of cost_units over the events whose event_type belongs to one flow, taken once for each flow in concept.flow_customer_order_to_provisioning, concept.flow_alarm_storm_to_incident_correlation, concept.flow_topology_lookup_to_ai_recommendation, and concept.flow_approved_remediation_to_validation.
metrics.today: docs/12-finops/cost-per-workflow.md states the cost for each of the four flows from events.jsonl. The money unit of cost_units is Unknown, so the figures are EDUCATIONAL.
